concerns.text: T007 implements a dynamic sample size reduction strategy (aborting if N < 100) which directly contradicts FR-001 and SC-005. The spec mandates a fixed sample size of 800 functions to ensure statistical validity. A task that allows the sample to drop below 100 (or even 800) without explicit spec authorization for 'staged' reduction is a semantic weakening of the requirement.

T014 specifies loading 'TheBloke/CodeLlama-Instruct-GGUF', whereas FR-004 and the Spec explicitly mandate 'CodeLlama-7B-Instruct-GGUF'. This introduces an unverified external artifact (different repository/user) violating Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and Principle IV (Single Source of Truth). The task silently relaxes the data source constraint.

T025 defines the sensitivity sweep range as abstract 'LOC ∈ {low, medium, high}', whereas FR-009 explicitly requires sweeping specific numeric thresholds 'LOC ∈ {50, 100, 150}'. This is a semantic weakening of the acceptance criteria; the deliverable cannot be verified against the spec without the specific numeric values.

T025c implements a Pearson correlation for SC-002, but SC-002 explicitly requires measuring the correlation 'against the logistic regression model coefficients'. The task explicitly forbids using regression coefficients ('Do NOT use regression coefficients'), thereby failing to satisfy the acceptance criterion defined in the spec.

T016 hardcodes a batch size of ≤10. While the Plan justifies this for RAM, FR-008 and Constitution Principle VI require recording metrics for 'every batch of ≤50 functions' to verify compliance with the hardware constraint. The task implements a restricted subset (10) without explicitly preserving the logic or verification path for the full 50-capacity constraint mandated by the spec, risking a silent drift in the validation scope.
